beginner.headline: Anthropic Stops AI Being Used for Bad Things
beginner.brief: Anthropic is an AI company. It said it stopped people from using its AI. They tried to make biological weapons. This information is in a report from the company. Other groups used AI for internet scams and bad actions. They also used AI to make software for other weapons. Anthropic will work to stop these bad activities in the future.

intermediate.headline: Anthropic Blocks AI Attempts to Create Biological Weapons
intermediate.brief: Anthropic has identified and disrupted attempts to use its AI model for "malicious activity" linked to biological weapons. The company's threat intelligence report includes revelations about these dangerous activities. This follows warnings from a former top researcher about the potential risks of AI to humanity. Claude, Anthropic's AI model, was also used by actors linked to a Russia-based cyber espionage campaign. Other cases of concern ranged from fake dating apps to surveillance built to identify dissidents. Anthropic also blocked scientists who used its AI in ways that could support biological weapons development. Biological misuse is considered "one of the most serious risks of frontier AI model" because it "could have catastrophic consequences" without proper safeguards. The company noted that the same information used for biological weapons can also develop vaccines or disease cures. Anthropic is incorporating these findings into its processes to better prevent and disrupt similar activities in the future.

advanced.headline: Anthropic Thwarts AI Misuse, Including Biological Weapon Attempts
advanced.brief: Anthropic says it has identified and disrupted attempts to use its AI model for "malicious activity" which could support the development of biological weapons. The revelations in Anthropic's threat intelligence report come after a former top researcher at the company warned of the risks of AI to humanity. The findings, made in the firm's recent threat intelligence report, are the latest in a growing series of warnings from AI researchers and industry insiders about the technology's potential risks to humanity. The cases of concern detected over the past eight months ranged from fake dating apps and hotel Wifi scams to surveillance built to identify dissidents. Claude, Anthropic's AI model, was also used by actors linked to a Russia-based cyber espionage campaign and by an Iranian propaganda institution, according to its report. This includes Google, which wrote on Tuesday that a person had attempted to use its AI tool, Gemini, to obtain a "complete, step-by-step technical guide for synthesizing weaponised biological agents". The lengthy report lists cases in which suspected state-sponsored groups, criminals, spyware vendors, state propaganda institutions, and politically motivated individuals misused its technology. Jacob Klein, the head of threat intelligence at Anthropic, told the New York Times it was "an incredibly nuanced situation". Anthropic stated, "The same information that can be used to develop a biological weapon could also be used to develop, for example, a vaccine or a cure for a disease." The report comes after a top safety researcher at Anthropic warned AI is advancing so quickly he believes there is a greater than 10% chance it "could kill all humans" within the next decade. In an article published on 6 September, OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki called for the industry to implement "voluntary slowdowns" until safeguards are set. In the US, Democratic lawmaker Bernie Sanders has introduced legislation to ban AI superintelligence and temporarily pause advanced AI development. Sanders emphasized, "When scientists tell you there is a chance, a chance that it could have a cataclysmic impact on humanity, you've got be a moron not to say, slow it down." The California-based company said it had incorporated its findings into its processes "to better prevent, detect, and disrupt these activities in the future". Anthropic also said it had shared intelligence with authorities and industry partners where appropriate.
